about: Default share of the monthly payment Social Security withholds to recover an overpayment, by the date the notice was sent. The rate printed on the person's own notice governs.

rows.rate: 10% of the monthly benefit or $10, whichever is more
rows.plain: For overpayment notices sent before March 27, 2025, Social Security's default was to withhold 10% of the monthly benefit or $10, whichever is more. The rate printed on your notice is the one that applies to you.
For overpayment notices sent from March 27, 2025, Social Security announced a default of withholding 100% of the monthly benefit. It changed this to 50% for notices sent from April 25, 2025.

For retirement, survivor and disability overpayment notices sent on or after April 25, 2025, Social Security's default is to withhold 50% of the monthly benefit if you do not repay, ask for a lower rate, appeal or ask for a waiver. You can ask for a lower rate with form SSA-634.
For SSI, Social Security withholds 10% of the monthly payment by default. The 2025 change to 50% did not apply to SSI.
